pr_title: do not remove volume dir when saveVolumeData fails
pr_body:

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug


**What this PR does / why we need it**:
If saveVolumeData() fails，all data in the volume dir is removed. This will happen when the disk is readonly and the volume is a remote disk.
```Go
    if err := saveVolumeData(dataDir, volDataFileName, volData); err != nil {
		if removeErr := os.RemoveAll(dataDir); removeErr != nil {
			klog.Error(log("failed to remove dir after error [%s]: %v", dataDir, removeErr))
		}
		return nil, errors.New(log("failed to save volume info data: %v", err))
	} 
```
There is no need to remove all in volume dir. When saveVolumeData fails, just log an error is enough because kubelet will retry to write volDataFileName next time.

issue_context.title: It is dangerous to call os.RemoveAll() when saveVolumeData() fails is csi NewMounter()
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When saveVolumeData() fails，dataDir is removed, and all data is gone.
``` go
	if err := saveVolumeData(dataDir, volDataFileName, volData); err != nil {
		if removeErr := os.RemoveAll(dataDir); removeErr != nil {
			klog.Error(log("failed to remove dir after error [%s]: %v", dataDir, removeErr))
		}
		return nil, errors.New(log("failed to save volume info data: %v", err))
	}

	klog.V(4).Info(log("mounter created successfully"))
```
This bug will happen when saveVolumeData() fails(in our environment, the disk is readonly). And the code is introduced in 2018. So most of the k8s environments are in the threaten of this bug.

**What you expected to happen**:
The data in mount point shouldn't be deleted.

comments: /assign
/sig node

What problem did you encounter w.r.t. the code cited above ?

thanks

@tedyu 
When encounter error, all files in `mount` directory will be deleted.

Step 1, csi mount ok
Step 2, kubelet restart, and call those code
Step 3, encounter error(disk quota exceed or disk readonly and so on), clean all data in csi mount.
@vladimirvivien Do you known the reason why to call os.RemoveAll() when saveVolumeData() fails?
/sig storage

From my point of view, I suggest to directly return error if `saveVolumeData` failed, because it seems calling os.RemoveAll or os.Remove is meaningless. And more, in fact we don't really need save volume data file every time if there is no changed contents.
